LESSON: READING 1.2.1 READING FOR INFORMATION: NOTE MAKING

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.2: Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Information: Note Making

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Information: Note Making. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why do we make notes?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify key points in a text for information
2. appreciate the role of making summaries in reading

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE LEARNING: READING 1.2.1 READING FOR INFORMATION: NOTE MAKING
This lesson teaches Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Information: Note Making for Grade 6 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

STUDY STEPS
1. identify key points in a text for information
   Practise this until you can do it without help.
2. appreciate the role of making summaries in reading
   Practise this until you can do it without help.

HOW TO SHOW UNDERSTANDING
Explain the idea in your own words, give one Kenyan example, then complete the practice tasks.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Describe Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Information: Note Making using something at your school.

Example 2: Give a home/community example from your county.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Underline the key ideas about Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Information: Note Making above.
2. Explain Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Information: Note Making to a parent using one local example.
3. Write or draw three things that prove you understand Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Information: Note Making.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Information: Note Making with school or home examples.
2. Answer: Why is Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Information: Note Making important for a Grade 6 learner?
3. Prepare a one-minute oral presentation for a parent or teacher.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do we make notes?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. identify key points in a text for information
2. appreciate the role of making summaries in reading

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
